speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying the timeline: when did the double vision and upper limb weakness first begin, and has it been progressive? Additionally, do you experience any difficulty swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty closing your eyes recently? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies combined with your symptoms of ptosis, diplopia that worsens with upgaze, and fluctuating weakness that improves with rest is diagnostic. I recommend requesting images of your chest to rule out an associated thymoma. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT
